name: Sydney Opera House
clue: White concrete shells, all cut from one imaginary sphere, sit on a harbour point. Its architect resigned mid-build and never came back to see it finished.

name: Eiffel Tower
clue: Built as a temporary gateway to a world's fair, this wrought-iron lattice was the tallest structure on Earth for 41 years.

name: Burj Khalifa
clue: Its Y-shaped plan is borrowed from a desert flower, and it has held the world height record since the day it opened.

name: Colosseum
clue: Four storeys of arches held around 50,000 spectators; sailors worked the canvas awning that shaded them.

name: Taj Mahal
clue: A white marble tomb for a beloved wife at the end of a quartered garden on a river bank. Its four minarets lean slightly outwards, away from the dome.

name: Empire State Building
clue: An Art Deco tower thrown up in just over a year during the Depression. Its mast was meant to moor airships.

name: Sagrada Família
clue: A basilica under construction since 1882. Its architect, knocked down by a tram, is buried in the crypt.

name: St Basil's Cathedral
clue: Nine chapels under swirling, candy-painted onion domes, at the end of the most famous square in a northern capital.

name: Petronas Towers
clue: Twin towers on an eight-pointed Islamic star plan, joined by a two-storey skybridge at the 41st and 42nd floors.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
clue: A cathedral bell tower started on soft clay. Wars stopped work for nearly a century, which let the ground settle and probably saved it from falling over.

name: Parthenon
clue: A marble Doric temple with almost no straight lines: the columns swell and the floor bows upwards to correct the eye.

name: Elizabeth Tower (Big Ben)
clue: A Gothic Revival clock tower on a riverside parliament. The name everyone uses really belongs to the 13-tonne bell inside.

name: Forbidden City
clue: Nearly a thousand red-and-gold buildings behind a moat. For five centuries, ordinary people could not enter without the emperor's permission.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
clue: A Gothic cathedral on a river island, with flying buttresses and rose windows. Its 19th-century spire fell in a 2019 fire and was rebuilt exactly.

name: Pantheon
clue: Still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, nearly 1,900 years on, with an open eye at the top that lets the rain in.

name: CN Tower
clue: A concrete telecom tower on a lakeshore, with a glass floor 342 m up. It was the world's tallest free-standing structure for 32 years.

name: Hagia Sophia
architect: Isidore of Miletus & Anthemius of Tralles
clue: A dome that seems to float on a ring of 40 windows. It has been a church, a mosque, a museum and a mosque again.

name: Marina Bay Sands
clue: Three 55-storey hotel towers carry a 340-metre 'park' across their roofs, with an infinity pool at the edge.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
clue: Titanium-clad curves on an old industrial riverfront. Its success gave a whole urban-regeneration strategy its name.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
clue: A fairy-tale castle for a reclusive king, secretly built on a steel frame with central heating. He lived there for only 172 days.

name: Fallingwater
clue: A weekend house whose concrete terraces cantilever straight out over a waterfall in the Appalachian woods.

name: Villa Savoye
clue: A white box on thin columns outside a capital, built as a manifesto of five points. A car's turning circle shaped the ground floor.

name: Chrysler Building
clue: A steel sunburst crown. Its spire was assembled in secret inside the top floors and hoisted out in 90 minutes to steal a height record.

name: Lotus Temple
clue: A Bahá'í house of worship made of 27 free-standing marble 'petals', open to people of every faith.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
clue: More than 80 white marble domes, reflecting pools, and one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world inside.

name: Atomium
clue: Nine steel spheres arranged as an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times, built for a world's fair.

name: Alhambra
clue: The red hilltop palace-fortress of the last Muslim kingdom in Western Europe, with honeycomb stucco ceilings and a fountain carried by twelve lions.

name: Potala Palace
clue: Thirteen storeys of white and red walls climbing a hill at 3,700 m: for three centuries the winter palace of a line of spiritual leaders.

name: Angkor Wat
clue: The largest religious monument on Earth. It faces west, and its five lotus-bud towers are mirrored in a vast moat.

name: CCTV Headquarters
clue: Two leaning towers joined at the top and bottom into one continuous loop for a state broadcaster. Locals call it 'big pants'.

name: Oslo Opera House
clue: Its white stone roof slopes down into a fjord, so anyone can walk straight up onto it.

name: Elbphilharmonie
clue: A glass crown shaped like waves, sitting on top of a brick cocoa warehouse in a port. The main hall is lined with 10,000 unique acoustic panels.

name: Cathedral of Brasília
clue: Sixteen curved concrete columns reach up like hands, in a capital city drawn from scratch in the 1950s.

name: Taipei 101
clue: Stacked like bamboo in eight-floor segments, with a 660-tonne golden steel ball hanging inside to calm typhoon sway.

name: Habitat 67
clue: 354 prefabricated concrete boxes stacked like a hillside village for a world expo — a student's thesis made real.

name: Kunsthaus Graz
clue: A blue acrylic blob with nozzle-shaped skylights, nicknamed 'the friendly alien', moored beside a red-roofed old town.

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
clue: A white surface that rises out of the plaza and folds over a cultural centre with almost no straight lines, near an inland sea.

name: National Parliament House (Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban)
clue: Massive concrete walls pierced by giant circles and triangles, standing in an artificial lake. Its architect died years before it was finished.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
clue: The largest mud-brick building in the world. Every year the whole town turns out in a festival to replaster it.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
clue: A concrete church whose stepped front imitates basalt columns formed by cooling lava, towering over a small capital.

name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
clue: A flying saucer on a cliff, reached by a red serpentine ramp, looking across a bay at a much more famous city.

name: Church of St George (Bete Giyorgis)
architect: Commissioned by King Gebre Mesqel Lalibela
clue: Carved downwards out of solid volcanic rock in the shape of a cross. It stands in its own pit, about 12 metres deep.

name: Jewish Museum Berlin
clue: A zinc-clad zigzag slashed with window cuts, with empty 'voids' inside that you can see into but never enter.

name: Turning Torso
clue: Nine five-storey cubes twist through 90 degrees up a 190-metre tower, based on its architect's sculpture of a human body.

name: Bosco Verticale
clue: Two apartment towers with around 900 trees planted on their balconies — a forest stood on end.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
clue: A 99-metre gilded stupa whose tip is set with thousands of diamonds; it is said to hold strands of the Buddha's hair.

name: Hassan II Mosque
clue: Its 210-metre minaret is one of the tallest in the world, part of the prayer hall stands over the ocean, and the roof slides open.

name: Zeitz MOCAA
wiki: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa
clue: Galleries carved out of the 42 concrete tubes of an old grain silo on a harbour waterfront.

name: Transitional Cathedral (Cardboard Cathedral)
clue: A church built from giant cardboard tubes after an earthquake wrecked the city's old cathedral. Meant to be temporary, still standing.

name: Yoyogi National Gymnasium
clue: Swooping roofs hung from steel cables like a suspension bridge, built for an Olympic swimming pool.
